newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Lloyd's chief plans Singapore expansion.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's chief plans Singapore expansion.

text.p: The Lloyd's of London insurance market is negotiating to expand its presence in Singapore, its chairman told Reuters Financial Television on Wednesday.
"We have been in discussions in Singapore," Sir David Rowland said from Tokyo in an interview. "They are not concluded and the conditions there may offer us fresh opportunities."
Lloyd's current Singapore presence is a representative office of its aviation department with minimal staffing.
Lloyd's underwrites risks in Singapore placed through approved brokers and underwriting agents.
Rowland gave no indication of the size of the market Lloyd's thought it could capture in Asia through a bigger presence in Singapore, or when a full service local office might be opened.

"My timeline is tomorrow and the day after that and the day after that always, because I'm very anxious we should build our business in as many areas which offer the opportunity for good profitable insurance underwriting and the conditions change from time to time," he said.

But generating premium was not dependent on establishing a physical presence in a given location, Rowland said. He added that Lloyd's syndicates were already underwriting reinsurance, marine and aviation risks located in Singapore.
Lloyd's Asia-Pacific gross premiums were about 574 million stg in 1995, the latest figures available. Globally, Lloyd's gross premiums were 8.9 billion stg.

About 30 percent of this total was generated by North American operations -- Lloyd's traditional stronghold in international insurance and reinsurance underwriting -- but Lloyd's was determined to broaden its earnings base.
"I want to maintain our U.S. business, but I want to see it balanced with growth elsewhere," Rowland said.
